chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Chapter 419 – Li Huowang Questions Reality Itself
chapter_meta_description: In a quiet but devastating chapter, Li Huowang returns to the hospital and faces a terrifying possibility: what if this world is real? A moment of warmth becomes a prison.
og_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch. 419 – Revisited Reality
og_description: Li Huowang reaches for sunlight and wonders if he’s been fighting the wrong fight.
twitter_description: No monsters. Just a man, a barred window, and the unbearable weight of a single sunbeam.

lore_anchors.definition: In Daoist internal alchemy, the primal cosmic energy that exists before the division of yin and yang. Tapping into it grants the ability to shape reality itself — the ultimate source of a Heart-Element’s dangerous power.
A rare human constitution in the Dao-Twisted World that makes a person a living conduit for Primordial One Qi. Their very existence blurs the line between belief and reality.

A secret society whose name means "The Way of Sitting in Forgetfulness." They are dedicated liars and tricksters who weaponize uncertainty and delight in collapsing the distinction between truth and falsehood.
The Zuowandao operative Li Huowang was pursuing before being pulled back into the hospital reality. His almost-capture represents the last thread of concrete action Li Huowang had in the other world.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why can’t Li Huowang produce gold in the modern world?
cultural_notes_faq.a: His failure to will gold or move objects with his mind is a key piece of evidence for his own doubt — it suggests his Heart-Element ability either doesn’t function in this reality, or he has no conscious control over it.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Is the modern world actually real?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The novel deliberately leaves this ambiguous. The chapter presents Li Huowang’s speculation, but no definitive proof is given — the horror is the uncertainty itself.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is Yang Na’s significance in this chapter?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Yang Na’s depression grounds Li Huowang’s cosmic paranoia in a real, personal wound. It shows that the emotional costs of his condition aren’t limited to the fantasy-horror world.
